pages.lesson:
LESSON: AREA

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements 3.2 Length (6 lessons) • Conversions in length • Operations in leng
Topic 3.3: Area

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Area. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: What are plane figures?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the relationship between square metre (m2 ) and hectares as units of measuring area

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Area.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Area using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Critical thinking and Problem-solving: as the learner cuts out the circle into small sectors, joining them to create a rectangle and generate a formula for getting the area of a circle.
2. Creativity and Imagination: as the learner combines different shapes to make patterns.
3. Self-efficacy: as the learner demonstrates how to derive the formula for the area of a circle. Values
4. Responsibility: as the learner cuts out the small sectors of the circle and joins them up to form a rectangle.
5. Integrity: as the learner works out exact areas of different shapes.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are plane figures?
2. How do we work out the areas of plane figures?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Area is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
